title: Minimum allocation guarantees and soft-eviction policy for Dedicated pools (PRD)
creator: Asha Patel
description: Provide tenant-level minimum allocation guarantees (a configurable floor) inside Dedicated GPU pools and implement a soft-eviction mechanism that gracefully reclaims burst capacity when contention occurs. The feature aims to give customers predictable baseline throughput while allowing controlled, reversible bursting with clear isolation and billing semantics.
goals: Allow operators to configure a guaranteed minimum % of pool capacity per tenant (alloc floor) to ensure steady baseline throughput for critical tenants
Implement soft-eviction flow that throttles or temporarily pauses non-critical burst workloads when pool usage exceeds safe thresholds instead of hard preemption
Expose administration controls and observability (Console + API) for floors, current usage vs guaranteed, and eviction events
Define deterministic billing and quota interplay between minimum guarantees and burst consumption
non_goals: This PRD does not cover cross-region failover or automatic tenant migration between pools
Not implementing preemptive kernel-level eviction for individual GPU processes (this is application-level request routing/throttling)
Does not change existing Dedicated reservation purchase flow (billing/commit model remains)
requirements: Config: per-pool 'alloc_floor' as percentage (0-100) and optional 'protected_tenants' list
Runtime: admission controller that nominates requests as 'guaranteed' or 'burst' based on tenant allocation and remaining pool capacity
Burst policy: configurable prioritization tiers (critical, best-effort) and soft-eviction thresholds at pool-level (e.g., 85%/95%)
Eviction action: non-disruptive throttling first (delayed scheduling or reduced concurrency), progress to short pause windows if necessary; allow immediate rollback when capacity returns
Metrics: per-tenant guaranteed_alloc, current_alloc, burst_consumed, eviction_events (count, duration), and evicted_request_ids
Console: UI to view and edit alloc_floor, see live allocation heatmap, and replay recent eviction incidents
API: endpoints to set/query alloc_floor and to subscribe to eviction webhook events
Audit: record any change to alloc_floor and any eviction decision to tenant audit logs
Acceptance tests: integration tests that simulate contention and validate guaranteed baseline remains available for protected tenants
acceptance_criteria: Given a pool with alloc_floor configured, guaranteed tenants retain access to at least their floor percentage of pool throughput under synthetic contention scenarios (measured at request completion rate)
When pool usage crosses soft_eviction_threshold, non-critical burst requests are throttled or delayed before any hard preemption occurs
Eviction events are recorded and visible in Console and via API with tenant, affected request ids, reason, and duration
Operators can update alloc_floor via Console or API and changes are audited with actor and timestamp
Billing reports clearly separate usage covered by guarantees vs burst overage and align with current billing model for Dedicated
No p99 latency regressions for guaranteed tenants compared to baseline under defined test workloads (<=5% relative p99 regression)
End-to-end integration test suite reproduces a contention scenario and asserts recovery within configured rollback window
design_notes: We will implement alloc_floor as a soft guarantee enforced by the request router and capacity admission controller rather than changing kernel-level scheduling. The runtime maintains a per-pool allocation ledger updated atomically on request start/stop. Soft-eviction uses progressive remedial stages: 1) backpressure to SDKs (429 with Retry-After when supported), 2) schedule delay (queueing with priority inversion), 3) short suspend windows for non-critical requests. This keeps customer workloads intact and simplifies rollback. We need careful coordination with batching and KV cache accounting to avoid double-counting tokens.
rollout_plan: Week 1: Prototype admission controller with simulated pool scheduler in staging; smoke test with synthetic workload
Week 2-3: Implement console controls and API surface; internal dogfood with 3 internal tenants on a dedicated pool
Week 4: Expand canary to selected paying customers with explicit opt-in; monitor metrics and incident channels
Week 5: Full rollout behind feature flag for all Dedicated pools, enable gradual percentage-based enforcement
Post-rollout: 2-week observation window, rollback plan prepared if customer-impacting regressions are detected
open_questions: Should alloc_floor support absolute vCPU/GPU units in addition to percentage? (ops ask for absolute for large mixed pools)
Do we expose an API to temporarily override alloc_floor during incidents? (security/ops trade-off)
How should caching of KV/prefixes be counted against floor guarantees when a tenant reuses large caches?
What's the expected billing label and rate for burst consumption—same as existing overage or separate SKU? Finance input required
decisions: Enforce guarantees at admission-controller layer (not OS/kernel)
Implement soft-eviction with progressive steps; no hard preemption at v1
Expose configuration as percentage on pool and protected_tenants whitelist
Audit logs required for both config changes and eviction actions
